reviewedBy: Claude Opus 5 — gave the 113 photos that had no URL an address, and stopped the sitemap listing pages twice
method: Measured against production data through a preview build, not read from source. Before: image_key is the camera frame name and DSC numbers reset per card, so 113 keys named two photos each across 6 albums (album pHqw25 shares numbers with 5 others). The sitemap emitted image_key blindly, so those 113 URLs appeared TWICE in a file whose job is to tell a crawler what exists once — and the second photo of each pair had no URL at all: /photo/DSC05553 could only reach one of them, and which one was undefined because the lookup had no ORDER BY. After: the sitemap has 20,921 URLs and 20,921 distinct URLs, zero duplicates. Verified 15 of the 113 pairs end to end through the rendered page: both members return 200, serve different photos (distinct cf_image_id in og:image) and declare different canonicals. /photo/DSC05553 and /photo/TRoiyO-DSC05553 are now two pages about two photos instead of one page and one orphan. Also verified /photo/DSC09999xxx and /photo/null still 404 rather than resolving to something. Separately, every one of the 20,655 lastmod values was invalid: W3C Datetime requires a timezone designator on any form carrying a time (verified against w3.org/TR/NOTE-datetime, which states the components 'must be present'), and these read 2026-01-29T18:48:49.846521 with none. Now emitted as YYYY-MM-DD, a complete W3C form needing no timezone; 0 of 20,655 invalid. The 13 albums absent from the sitemap were checked rather than assumed — all 13 are visibility=unlisted private client sessions (portraits, graduations, a proposal), correctly excluded.
